annotations.target_phrase: Mr Leopold Bloom ate with relish the inner organs of beasts and fowls.
annotations.annotation_text: The iconic opening sentence of Part II (The Odyssey) and Episode 4 (Calypso), introducing Leopold Bloom at 8:00 AM in the kitchen of 7 Eccles Street. Immediately establishes Bloom's earthy, visceral, and sensuous humanity in contrast to Stephen Dedalus's scholastic asceticism.
sources: Gilbert, Stuart. James Joyce's Ulysses: A Study. Faber & Faber, 1930.
Ellmann, Richard. James Joyce. Oxford University Press, 1982.
Gifford, Don, and Robert J. Seidman. Ulysses Annotated. UC Press, 1988.

annotations.target_phrase: grilled mutton kidneys which gave to his palate a fine tang of faintly scented urine
annotations.annotation_text: Key anatomical correspondence for Calypso: the Kidney (organ). Joyce foregrounds somatic biology and gastrointestinal reality, evoking Homer's epic feasts through the modest breakfast of a Dublin advertising canvasser.
sources: Gifford, Don. Ulysses Annotated. UC Press, 1988, p. 70.
Kenner, Hugh. Ulysses. Johns Hopkins University Press, 1987.
